items.title: Labarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: The interviewer mentions Quincy Jones in a documentary context; the interviewee responds by discussing their own arranging philosophy and mentions Henry Mancini, but provides no personal interaction or specific relationship with Quincy Jones.

ctx.x: Oh yeah, we had to go take tap dance lessons after that. It didn’t last very long, I couldn’t stand it.

So a while back I watched, it was a pretty good documentary on Quincy Jones. But I was disappointed that no one asked him where do your arranging ideas come from. It was mostly just people saying, you know, how great he was and his whole resume, which is incredible. So my question to you is, can you tell me where your arranging ideas, how do they occur to you?

The song does it. You take the song that you’re arranging and that tells you everything. It gives you everything you need. It really does. You know you can change — rhythmically or harmonically you’ve got all the material to work with. And every now — well maybe it’s just the talent, but I’ll go through, first of all I play through the song and listen to it, and then something will spring out, like oh here’s a good introduction or here’s a good shout chorus or you know, something in that melody, because that’s…
